title: Normalized open restriction comparison for the published quotient Roos completion
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l, an open immersion e:V→W, any normalized integral open Operations o [def-sf-integral-open-operations], and an adic coefficient datum whose ideal is generated by the specified uniformizer [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Site and coefficient universes are independent. The finite coefficient maps and completed map of o are isomorphisms, and its finite maps commute with all quotient transitions. For the actual quotient Roos completion and unit [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], there are natural isomorphisms rho:completion_W⋙star_o≅star_o⋙completion_V and c from qGood_W⋙completion_W⋙star_o to the tower on W restricted termwise and then sent through the signed Roos functor and Q [def-sf-strict-roos-functor]. The square star_o(eta_W) followed by rho equals eta_V on every derived object. On every good representative P, star_o(eta_W(QP)) followed by c_P equals the exact-derived restriction factor followed by Q of restriction(roosUnit_W(P)) followed by scalarRoosMap on the quotient tower [def-sf-additive-roos-map]. No finiteness, boundedness or completeness assumption on the derived object is imposed.

source.place: Tag 099N (2),(5), proof of lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case; Tag 0941; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 0G7E and 07A4 for strict tensor normalization.

proof.text: Use the proved finiteMap_eq and completedMap_eq normalization equalities from OpenRestrictionGoodComplex to obtain isomorphisms. The existing finiteTransportSquare lemma derives the quotient-transition equations directly from naturality of the supplied normalized systemMap and its systemComponents; no unfolding of constant sheafification is needed.

Use the ordinary augmented quotient-tower comparison for the prescribed Operations. The ordinary restriction is a right adjoint, hence preserves countable products. The generic restrictionRoosIsIso lemma makes scalarRoosMap an isomorphism. Its naturality assembles these into a natural Roos comparison. Compose the published completionComparison and exact-derived restriction factor to define c.

Restriction preserves good complexes. Lift its termwise functor to the full good subcategories. Compose c with Roos of the ordinary quotient-tower isomorphism and the inverse target completionComparison. Fully faithful whiskering along qGood lifts this natural isomorphism to rho.

Use the already proved generic augmentedRoosMap helper from IsomorphismOrdinaryCompletionChain (its statement has no geometric isomorphism assumption). Its two mapping-cocone coordinates reduce the chain augmentation equation to the quotient augmentation square and the zero shifted coordinates. The representative normalization of completionUnit and naturality of the exact-derived restriction factor give the displayed c equation. Cancel the target representative isomorphism, use this strict augmentation identity, and apply faithfulness of whiskering to obtain the all-object rho unit equation.

proof_origin.place: Tag 099N (5); cokernel construction of the ordinary quotient comparison, signed Roos product comparison, and resolving-class localization. All chain, coefficient, derived descent and unit-compatibility steps are proved in Lean.

theorem restrictionDescent
    (_d : AdicCoefficientDatum (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E))
    (_hd : _d.ideal = Ideal.span {Padic.coefficientExtensionUniformizer l E}) :
(∀ n : ℕ, IsIso (o.finiteMap n)) ∧ IsIso o.completedMap ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ,
        o.finiteMap (n + 1) ≫
          ((IntegralOpenReduction.sliceSite e).sheafPushforwardContinuous
            CommRingCat.{max u (t + 1)} ((ProEt.topology W).over
              (IntegralOpenReduction.openObject e)) (ProEt.topology V)).map
                (coefficientSequenceCommRingTransition l E V n) =
        ((ProEt.topology W).overPullback CommRingCat.{max u (t + 1)}
          (IntegralOpenReduction.openObject e)).map
            (coefficientSequenceCommRingTransition l E W n) ≫ o.finiteMap n) ∧
    ∃ (rho : IntegralOnSlice.completion l E W none ⋙ IntegralOpenReduction.star l E e o ≅
        IntegralOpenReduction.star l E e o ⋙ IntegralOnSlice.completion l E V none)
      (c : IntegralOnSlice.qGood l E W none ⋙
          (IntegralOnSlice.completion l E W none ⋙ IntegralOpenReduction.star l E e o) ≅
        (IntegralOnSlice.Good l E W none).ι ⋙ IntegralOnSlice.tower l E W none ⋙
          (Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ _ _).obj
            ((IntegralOpenReduction.restriction l E e o).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)) ⋙
          integralOperationsRoosFunctor ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q),
      (∀ H : IntegralOnSlice.D l E W none,
        (IntegralOpenReduction.star l E e o).map
            ((IntegralOnSlice.completionUnit l E W none).app H) ≫ rho.hom.app H =
          (IntegralOnSlice.completionUnit l E V none).app
            ((IntegralOpenReduction.star l E e o).obj H)) ∧
      (∀ P : (IntegralOnSlice.Good l E W none).FullSubcategory,
        (IntegralOpenReduction.star l E e o).map
            ((IntegralOnSlice.completionUnit l E W none).app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.obj)) ≫
            c.hom.app P =
          (IntegralOpenReduction.restriction l E e o).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app P.obj ≫
            DerivedCategory.Q.map
              (((IntegralOpenReduction.restriction l E e o).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map
                  (IntegralOnSlice.roosUnit l E W none P.obj) ≫
                scalarRoosMap (IntegralOpenReduction.restriction l E e o)
                  ((IntegralOnSlice.tower l E W none).obj P.obj)))
